title: MZ The Hidden Art of Innkeeping - out now on Steam and Itch.io!

posts.author: SeaPhoenix
posts.body:
Release date: Sep 3, 2024
Now available on
Steam
and
Itch.io
for US$7.99 with a weeklong 10% launch discount!!
​
Synopsis
Welcome to the south coast, where beautiful beaches and sunny days abound! Unfortunately, the only hotel in the area has enjoyed a monopoly for years and is notorious for its bad service and tiny, expensive rooms. After a disastrous stay, Elinor decides to take on the challenge of converting a dilapidated farmhouse in a small neighboring village into an inn.
Meet a colorful cast of characters as Elinor welcomes visitors to her new inn and recruits villagers and employees. While trying to meet her guests' finicky demands, she also has to contend with the machinations of the manager of the rival hotel. Moreover, renovating the inn doesn't come cheap, so she's forced to take a loan from an elderly tycoon who demands payment within a month.
Meanwhile, she discovers various objects hidden around the village and the surrounding areas, and gradually learns more about the other villagers and the mysterious former owner of the farmhouse. Can Elinor uncover the secrets of the past, revive the fortunes of the struggling village, and turn the inn into a roaring success before the deadline?
Highlights
Renovate the inn, and watch it transform from a decrepit farmhouse to a luxurious inn!
Meet unusual and fascinating guests, including biologists, adventurers, a pirate, and even a vampire - plus some familiar faces from
The Lost Art of Innkeeping
!
Discover new areas, welcome residents to the village, and unlock delicious dishes to be served to your guests!
Find items and beautiful paintings that will help you improve the inn as well as uncover the secrets of farmhouse's former owner.
Configure guest rooms, purchase amenities, hire employees, and upgrade the inn and its surroundings to keep your guests happy.
Complete mini-quests such as getting seeds for the farmer, restoring a ruined monastery, helping kids build a sand castle, and more!
Replay the game with a New Game+ and discover several exciting new items and guests, and experience different outcomes based on your choices and actions.
Unlock achievements, master the art of innkeeping, and become the owner of a 5-star inn that caters even to royalty!

posts.author: SeaPhoenix
posts.body:
Welcome to the Grand Hotel! This is the opening scene of
The Hidden Art of Innkeeping
, where Elinor's disastrous stay leads her to open a competing inn nearby, and it's one of the first maps I created for the game.
I thought it might be interesting to show how this map evolved (see spoiler below). I started with the idea of a big, imposing, and yet impersonal hotel by the beach with lots of rooms and an outdoor cafe area. Then, to give the impression that it's in a large city, I paved the area and added some shops and greenery.
Much later on, I added some people and movement to keep it vibrant, but now that I think about it, I'm going to add more people to this scene so that it looks uncomfortably crowded as well!
Spoiler:
Evolution of a beach hotel (GIF)

posts.author: SeaPhoenix
posts.body:
I'm trying to incorporate more visual changes in The Hidden Art of Innkeeping, to show how things get better at the inn as you progress through the game. After all, it's nice to know that one is making a difference!
At the start of the game, the kitchen is dirty and messy. There's a definite improvement after you clean it up and hire a chef! You can expand it and upgrade it even further later on but we'll save that for a future screenshot.
I also wanted to highlight an exciting new feature in The Hidden Art of Innkeeping: you get to choose what food to serve to your guests! Not only will the dishes add to your guests' happiness, some of the guests will have cravings for certain things (how about some cookies?) and they'll reward you if you serve it during their stay.
Needless to say, you'll get to unlock more dishes as you get to know the villagers, meet new people, and discover new areas. I hope this sounds fun!

The first step towards making a Steam store page though was making a trailer, and that took me forever! But I finally posted it on YouTube, and the Steam page should be up and running in a week or so:
The music in the trailer is "Keys for Success" by Darren Curtis.
One thing I learned from this process is that OBS Studio (a free, open-source recording and streaming software) is pretty good!

posts.author: SeaPhoenix
posts.body:
I'd like to highlight one of the buildings in The Hidden Art of Innkeeping - the lighthouse! Because this lighthouse would not have existed without
@Avery
, who has made and shared a ton of resources with the community.
I was looking up "picturesque lighthouses" on Google for my game, and came across Peggy's Cove Lighthouse in Nova Scotia, Canada. And it actually seemed possible for me to recreate it, by using the
lighthouse
made by Avery as a base, and recoloring the roof and fence. I made the
diagonal walls with the help of the following tutorials (also by Avery!):
Make Your Own Diagonal Walls!
Creating Your Own Roof Variations Part 2
(Photo of the lighthouse on the left by
KristaKals
)
The other elements of the lighthouse are edited from the FSM DLCs, as well as the Useful Window Glass Tiles DLC.
Of course, this is not the only instance where I'm using Avery's graphics - I'm a big fan of the
icons
as well, and you'll also see a number of other tiles by Avery in my game. So a big thank you to Avery!

posts.author: SeaPhoenix
SeaPhoenix
posts.body:
Hope 2024 is shaping up to be a good year for everyone!
As you might expect from the title,
The Hidden Art of Innkeeping
is going to have some hidden art. But that's not all that you'll find.
While you explore the village and the surroundings, you may come across some mysterious mounds of dirt. It turns out they contain buried artifacts, and you'll meet an archaeologist who can tell you more about them and their historical significance to the local area. (If you've played the prequel,
The Lost Art of Innkeeping
, you'll have a very good idea of who this archaeologist is.)
In addition, you'll be able to find books by a famous author scattered around the village - see if you can collect them all!
By the way, what I try to do in all my games is that the player can take items only if they don't seem to belong to anyone else, or if you have the owner's permission. This is based on a valuable life lesson I learned playing one of the Ultima games when I was very young: you can't just take things from people's houses! (The guards came after me after I happily looted everything in a village, which had seemed like a very normal thing to do in video games back then!)
I'm participating in Steam Next Fest on Feb 5-12, so I'll be releasing a demo for this game. The demo is going to be about 30 minutes long, and I've been busy putting the final touches on it. I finally had someone else playtest part of the game a couple days ago; this is the first time someone aside from me has actually played it and I always find that a little nerve-wracking, though it's useful to get feedback and see another perspective of the game.
Anyhow, you'll be able to try the demo on both Steam and Itch.io next month! I'll post the links when they're up.

posts.author: SeaPhoenix
posts.body:
I'm excited to announce that The Hidden Art of Innkeeping will be released on Sep 3, 2024 on
Steam
and
Itch
!
It's been about three years since I started working on this game. I had a lot of fun making it, and I really appreciated getting feedback from people who played the first game,
The Lost Art of Innkeeping
, and the demo too. It was especially useful hearing which characters people liked in the first game and wanted to see again in the sequel.
It was also a pleasure working with two artists: Fatti, who did the paintings, and
@hiddenone
, who created a number of the pixel art characters and did some really cute animations, including the one below based on the tiger sprite by
@whtdragon
:
The RPG Maker community has been great - I wouldn't be able to make this game without the many plugins and resources that people have shared, and I've learned a lot over the years from browsing through the posts here. I appreciate the many useful and supportive comments I've gotten from people here and on Reddit, and special thanks in particular to
@fizzly
,
@slimmmeiske2
, and
@hiddenone
for playtesting and for their feedback.
Anyway, I hope you're as excited as I am about the upcoming release! The demo will be available on
Steam
and
Itch
until the release of the game, so you can try it now! (Do note that you won't be able to use the savefiles from the demo in the released game, since some things have changed since I made the demo.)
